result.markdown:
If you're looking at **L. Frank Baum's original Oz books**, there are 14 novels, and a handful are generally considered standouts. Interestingly, some readers actually prefer the sequels to the famous first book.

Based on reader ratings, literary commentary, and fan rankings, here's how I'd narrow them down.

## The best Wizard of Oz books

![Ozma of Oz: Record of Her Adventures with Dorothy Gale of Kansas, the Yellow Hen, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, Tiktok, the Cowardly Lion and the Hungry Tiger; Besides Other Good People too Numerous to Mention Faithfully Recorded Herein by L. Frank Baum: Fair Hardcover | Reasons To Live Books](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/b4uqHO2aERnrzTXkUivYASpHWPO3YjpcCsnnsIZs59LdgF7zVOE_DN755uon0xFRojkMHxUS4UfIaWqXfyANOv-o9cArt5G62YnO9EIx4-Snh5jBv362VfysQaFJNphcBal0HPmHjgsSUZHqpV8DYhF2Qvs8O4bUcOEDVUo5oeZf3d4qXKukmBu8Y0B7XSf2?purpose=fullsize)

**1\. Ozma of Oz \(1907)**

(Best sequel pick)

Frequently ranked among the very best. Introduces memorable characters and expands the mythology of Oz. It is also the highest-rated volume in one comparative series ranking. **2\. The Wonderful Wizard of Oz \(1900)**

**6\. The Emerald City of Oz \(1910)**

Particularly interesting for readers who love the world-building. Explores Oz's society, geography, and inhabitants in greater depth. Gore Vidal also singled it out as a childhood favorite. [ultimatefantasyranking.com](https://ultimatefantasyranking.com/universes/oz.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[marveloustales.com](https://marveloustales.com/2014/05/28/the-ozma-trilogy/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.nybooks.com](https://www.nybooks.com/articles/1977/10/13/on-rereading-the-oz-books/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## What about the rest?

Other books worth considering\:

- **The Magic of Oz** \(1919) – imaginative later adventure.
- **Rinkitink in Oz** \(1916) – a somewhat different, fairy-tale-like adventure.
- **The Patchwork Girl of Oz** \(1913) – particularly whimsical and inventive.
- **Tik-Tok of Oz** \(1914) – another popular adventure featuring unusual characters.

## My recommendation

If you only want to read three, I'd choose\:

1. *The Wonderful Wizard of Oz*
2. *Ozma of Oz*
3. *The Scarecrow of Oz*

One interesting observation: Gore Vidal wrote a wonderful 1977 essay, *On Rereading the Oz Books*, discussing how the books hold up as adult literature. He even preferred some of the sequels to the original when he was young. **6\. The Emerald City of Oz \(1910)**

Particularly interesting for readers who love the world-building. Explores Oz's society, geography, and inhabitants in greater depth. Gore Vidal also singled it out as a childhood favorite. [ultimatefantasyranking.com](https://ultimatefantasyranking.com/universes/oz.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[marveloustales.com](https://marveloustales.com/2014/05/28/the-ozma-trilogy/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.nybooks.com](https://www.nybooks.com/articles/1977/10/13/on-rereading-the-oz-books/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## What about the rest?

Other books worth considering\:

- **The Magic of Oz** \(1919) – imaginative later adventure.
- **Rinkitink in Oz** \(1916) – a somewhat different, fairy-tale-like adventure.
- **The Patchwork Girl of Oz** \(1913) – particularly whimsical and inventive.
- **Tik-Tok of Oz** \(1914) – another popular adventure featuring unusual characters.

## My recommendation

If you only want to read three, I'd choose\:

1. *The Wonderful Wizard of Oz*
2. *Ozma of Oz*
3. *The Scarecrow of Oz*

One interesting observation: Gore Vidal wrote a wonderful 1977 essay, *On Rereading the Oz Books*, discussing how the books hold up as adult literature. He even preferred some of the sequels to the original when he was young.
